what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 2 of 3: On a causal event lattice, which formation clauses still matter?. GIVEN (refereed): on a finite causal DAG any two topological orders give the same joint law (product of kernels given parents); hypothesis: every predecessor recorded before its successor, no record re-formed. Referee's remark on a failed clause attempt: on level-ordered Z^3 two same-level sites are never nearest neighbours (the fork offset e_i - e_j has squared length 2), so joint formation of a same-level unit is exactly the product of the one-site kernels. The three clause attempts of round 1 had correct finite computations and FAILED at the interpretive step. TASK: a precise theorem and a precise list. (a) Theorem: for a causal event lattice, every formation-rate clause (clocks of any rates) and every formation-unit clause whose units are antichains induces the same law; prove it. (b) List exactly which clause candidates recorded in blocks 14, 15, 24 (PRs #8148, #8149, #8158) violate causality or re-form records, and for each give the smallest window where it changes the law, with the exact total-variation distance. (c) The unrecorded-site clause (block 24: free window against integrated exterior): does causality settle it? (d) Consequence: state what remains genuinely open about HOW records form once the event lattice is causal. ROUND 2: the first round's attempts and referee reports are under probes/work/derive/<problem>/ and logs/probes/J:derive:*/ and logs/probes/J:confirm:J-derive-*/ (python3 probes/harvest.py lists them); what survived refereeing is stated below as GIVEN, what failed is stated as the gap. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/causal-clauses/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route.
